newsitem.title: UK: GM, Renault UK venture creates 900 jobs.
newsitem.headline: GM, Renault UK venture creates 900 jobs.

text.p: U.S. car giant General Motors and France's Renault announced plans on Thursday to create 900 jobs in a 180 million pounds ($300.9 million) link-up to build a new medium-sized van range at a car plant in Luton, north of London.

The move will also safeguard 1,800 existing jobs at the IBC Vehicles plant. The UK's Department of Trade and Industry welcomed the investment as a sign of confidence in the British motor industry. "This is excellent news for IBC Vehicles and for Luton," said industry minister Greg Knight. It follows GM's UK unit Vauxhall announcing a 300 million pounds investment in its Ellsemere Port plant in northwest England in October.
Both groups are keen to boost their presence in this expanding marketplace, with industry analysts pointing out that similar partnerships between car-makers are flourishing.
Manufacturers are not concerned about the dilution of their strong brand-names in light commercial vehicles because styling is not so individual in this market sector.

The western European market for such vehicles, which includes pick-ups and small trucks, is put at 1.3 million sales per annum -- or one-tenth of the car market. The growth rate is six percent per annum.
